To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inactivation of Gsk3alpha in either liver or skeletal muscle has no effect on glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity in C57BL/ 6 mice.
the insulin sensitization observed in the global deletion of GSK3α is strain specific.
the insulin-sensitivity phenotype observed upon global deletion of GSK3α is mediated through a strain-specific, tissue-independent, mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the two isoform of GSK- 3 (GSK3α and Gsk3β) in glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie insulin resistance and Type-2 diabetes and the development of therapeutic strategies that can be used to ameliorate the disease state.
the role of glycogen synthetase kinase-3α (gsk-3α) as a regulator of insulin action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSK-3 isoform-specific deletion is tissue and strain dependent.
GSK-3 isoforms do not contribute significantly to glucose metabolism and insulin action in skeletal muscle and/or liver.
the GSK-3 isoforms are not the primary mediators of insulin action in the liver and muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inactivation of Gsk-3α does not improve insulin sensitivity or hepatic glucose metabolism, but rather the lack of insulin resistance and improved glucose homeostasis is a consequence of the genetic makeup and background of the mice.

GSK-3 is a key regulator of hepatic glucose production in the out-breed strain of mice and that the improved insulin-sensitivity observed upon global inactivating of GSK-α in this strain is likely to be mediated by indirect mechanisms.
GSK-3 is a promising target for the treatment of diabetes, but the isoforms and tissue specificity of GSK- 3 inhibition are likely to be crucial in determining the efficacy of any GSK-3 inhibitor
The main takeaway from our work is that

GSK-3 inhibition may be a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetes, however, the relative contributions of GSK-α and GSK3β to insulin sensitivity and hepato-glucose metabolism may be strain-dependent
the effects of GSK- 3 inhibition in vivo are likely to be complex, involving multiple tissue-specific and strain-specific effects.
the effects of GSK- 3 inhibitors on glucose and insulin sensitivity are likely to be mediated by off-target effects.
